caption:
The part people miss about Claude's text watermark: it isn't only for text Claude wrote.

Anthropic's own explainer says the mark indicates text was processed by Claude. Paste in a paragraph you wrote yourself for a proofread, a translation or a summary, and the output carries the mark. It travels with copy-paste and can persist through some editing. The EU has required providers serving its market to mark AI-generated content since 2 August 2026, and other major model developers signed the same code, so this won't stay a Claude-only thing.

Two things that make it less alarming. Anthropic says the watermark carries no identifying information and can't be traced back to a person, organisation or chat, and nothing hidden is inserted into your text.

So the move isn't to hide it. It's slide 4: a four-line AI-use note in the proposal, before delivery. A client who already knows how you work doesn't run detectors.

Not legal advice — and absence of a mark proves nothing either way.

Save this before your next handover. Has a client asked you the AI question yet?
